items.hook: News of the World is a 2020 American Western film co-written and directed by Paul Greengrass, based on the 2016 novel of the same name by Paulette Jiles, and starring Tom Hanks and introducing Helena Zengel in her international film debut.
items.body: The film follows an aging Civil War veteran who must return a young girl who was taken in by the Kiowa, and raised as one of them, to her last remaining family. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Climax of the Siege of Thessalonica by the Slavs in a three-day assault on the city walls.
items.body: The siege of Thessalonica in 676–678 was an attempt by the local Slavic tribes to capture the Byzantine city of Thessalonica, taking advantage of the preoccupation of the Byzantine Empire with the repulsion of the First Arab Siege of Constantinople. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: At the behest of Tsar Peter the Great, the construction of Kadriorg Palace, dedicated to his wife Catherine, begins in Tallinn.
items.body: Peter I was the Tsar of all Russia from 1682 and the first Emperor of Russia from 1721 until his death in 1725. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.body: New director will take over from Mia Bays in October.

items.hook: The Duke of Parma is defeated near the Dutch city of Nijmegen by an Anglo-Dutch force led by Maurice of Orange.
items.body: Alexander Farnese was an Italian noble and military leader, who was Duke of Parma, Piacenza and Castro from 1586 to 1592, as well as Governor of the Spanish Netherlands from 1578 to 1592. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Fred Urquhart or Frederick Burrows Urquhart was a Scottish short story writer, novelist, editor and reviewer.
items.body: He is considered Scotland's leading short story writer of the 20th century. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Seizure is the second novel in the Virals series of novels for young adults written by the American forensic anthropologist and crime writer, Kathy Reichs and her son Brendan Reichs, featuring Tory Brennan, great-niece of Temperance Brennan.
items.body: One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The Crossroads Baker device is the first underwater nuclear weapon test.
items.body: Operation Crossroads was a pair of nuclear weapon tests conducted by the United States at Bikini Atoll in mid-1946. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: French and Indian War: In Western New York, British forces capture Fort Niagara from the French, who subsequently abandon Fort Rouillé.
items.body: The French and Indian War (1754–1763) was a conflict in North America between Great Britain and France, along with their respective Indigenous allies, which were called "Indians" at the time. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: King Henry VI of England lays the foundation stone of King's College Chapel, Cambridge.
items.body: Henry VI was King of England from 1422 to 1461 and again from 1470 to 1471, and claimant to the French throne from 1422 to 1453 under the terms of the Treaty of Troyes. One of those things you can't un-know.
